newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates drop as repo cuts unseen.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates drop as repo cuts unseen.

text.p: Hungary's overnight rates dropped on abundant market liquidity, boosted by receding interest in central bank's one-week and one-month reverse repos, dealers said.
The overnight rates finished at 20.625 percent, down from 21 percent, extending a slide that was sparked by a recent National Bank of Hungary (NBH) rate hike which cooled repo rate cut expectations.

The rates moved from about 24 percent two weeks ago following a 0.25 percent surprise hike in the six-month deposit facility, which indicated that the NBH wanted to stop the interest rate decline trend of the past one year. Banks were confident that the market would remain liquid in the next few week as most of them were lenders in the first half of the two-week reserve period.
Dealers were divided on how the overnight rates would move next week, some saying it will ease and others that it will be flat.
"They will go down to levels around 20 percent next week," a dealer said.
"They will not move anywhere," another dealer said.
